text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

WHEAT SALE - Egypt's main grain buyer said on Sunday he was buying a total of 450,000 tonnes of French soft red wheat -- 100,000 tonnes at $167 FOB for loading in October and 300,000 tonnes at $163.90 FOB for loading in November. Another 50,000 tonnes of French soft red wheat was at $163.90 a tonne FOB, for loading any time in November, said Samir Shakankiri, vice chairman of the state's General Authority for Supply Commodities.

WHEAT TENDER - Morocco will tender on September 18 to import 35,000 tonnes of optional soft wheat for shipment in the first half of October, European grain traders said. Morocco seeks to import 15,000 tonnes of wheat between October 1 and October 10 to Nador and Tangiers and another 20,000 tonnes between October 5 and October 15 to Agadir, they said.
- The CCC seeks up to 42,000 tonnes of U.S.
No. 2 or better hard red winter wheat under the export donation program to Georgia. The shipment period is October 10-November 5 and offers are due by September 23.

WHEAT TENDERS - Syria's General Establishment for Cereal Processing and Trade offered 50,000 tonnes of hard amber durum wheat for sale. September 17 was set as the final date to receive price offers. Confirmation would be made on September 18, for shipment from Oct 15 to Nov 14.
Syria separately offered 100,000 tonnes of hard amber durum wheat for sale for November shipment. October 1 was final date for offers. Confirmation is set on October 2.
- The CCC seeks 25,000 tonnes of U.S. hard red winter wheat under the export donation program for Bosnia. Shipment is set for Oct 5-31 and bids are due on September 17.
WHEAT TENDERS - The CCC seeks up to 4,410 tonnes of U.S. No.2 soft red winter or soft white wheat for donation to Senegal for October 5-31 and offers are due by Sept 18.
- The CCC seeks 45,000 tonnes U.S. hard red winter wheat, maximum moisture 13.5 percent to donation for Ethiopia. Shipment set for November 1-25 and offers due by Sept 19.
CORN TENDER - Jordan is to seek 50,000 tonnes of U.S. Number 3 yellow corn for shipment in first half of November. Offers must be received by September 25.
- CCC seeks up to 4,280 tonnes of U.S. No.2 yellow corn to Angola. Shipment is for Oct 5-31 and offers due by Sept 18.

BARLEY TENDER - Syria's General Establishment for Cereal Processing and Trade is offering 100,000 tonnes of black feed barley from 1995 crops for sale. Occtober 15 was set as final date for price offers. Confirmation would be made on October 16. He said 50,000 tonnes would be ready for shipment in November and the remaining 50,000 tonnes in December.

RICE TENDER - The state-run Rice Export Corporation of Pakistan said it had invited fresh bids for the sale and export of 30,000 tonnes of 1995/96 (July-June) basmati rice including seven percent broken. An RECP official said bids should be submitted by Sunday.

RICE TENDER - The Republic of the Congo seeks to buy about 13,300 tonnes of U.S. long grain milled rice under the PL-480 Title I export program, its U.S. export buying agent said. Offers are due by 1400 EDT/1800 GMT Wednesday. Shipment is for November 5-20 and offers are to be quoted U.S. dollars free-alongside ship (FAS).

SOYBEAN OIL TENDER - The Republic of the Congo seeks to buy 3,400 tonnes of PL-480 tonnes of soybean oil delivered in 20-liter pails. Offers are due at the agent's Washington, D.C., office by Wednesday. Shipment is for November 5-20.

MARKET TALK - South Korea and Taiwan are expected to buy more than 400,000 tonnes of corn this week to take advantage of a fall in prices, traders said. The Koreans may buy 250,000 to 300,000 tonnes of Argentine corn while the Taiwanese would likely tender for at least 108,000 tonnes of corn, they said. The Korea Feed Association is seeking 35,000 tonnes of feed corn and 15,000 tonnes of feed barley on Tuesday.

... The large Egyptian purchase of French soft wheat is a signal U.S. wheat may be out of the pipeline for world export business, U.S. exporters said. "We are way overpriced in the world market and until we get that adjusted, it is going to be hard for us to capture business," one said.
